jobs.title: Human Resources Generalist
jobs.body:
Human Resources Generalist
Location: Fairlawn, Ohio or any of our OH offices. One is located in Medina! Travel to Fairlawn, OH about 1-2 times per month.
Employment Type: Full-Time, Hybrid

Position Summary

We are seeking a Human Resources Generalist to support the day-to-day operations of the HR department while continuing to build and broaden their HR expertise. In this role, you will provide foundational support across employee relations, talent acquisition, onboarding, HR administration, HRIS maintenance, compliance, and employee experience. Acting as an approachable resource for employees and managers, you will help ensure HR programs and policies are administered consistently, effectively, and in alignment with company values.

Working with the HR team, you will play an active role in talent development by helping coordinate university recruiting, attending career fairs, and supporting the day-to-day administration of our internship program. Additionally, you will support vital HR operations, including time and labor tracking, call-off administration, employee recognition initiatives, HRIS data accuracy, and backup payroll processing, helping maintain departmental continuity and deliver excellent service to the team.

Why Join Us?
Opportunity for long-term career growth and increasing responsibility as the HR department and organization expand.
Direct exposure to key HR functions, employee relations initiatives, talent acquisition strategies, and people operations.
A supportive, team-oriented culture where HR colleagues work together, share coverage, and celebrate team successes.
A positive work environment built on respect, accountability, continuous learning, and open communication.
Encouragement to bring forward fresh ideas, streamline HR processes, and leverage modern HRIS tech and automation.
Meaningful opportunity to make a direct impact on the employee experience and organizational culture while advancing your HR career.

Key Responsibilities
Recruitment, Internship Program & Onboarding
Support full-cycle recruiting: post positions, screen applicants, schedule interviews, coordinate background checks, and assist with offer and pre-employment administration and coordination.
Partner with hiring managers to maintain accurate, up-to-date job descriptions and hiring criteria.
Represent the organization at career fairs, university events, and community outreach functions to build talent pipelines.
Lead and administer the internship program, including recruitment, onboarding, manager support, engagement activities, and program evaluation.
Facilitate onboarding and new employee orientation, serving as an HR resource during introductory employment periods.
Facilitate onboarding activities and new employee orientation programs.
Serve as an HR resource for new hires during onboarding and introductory employment periods to promote a positive employee experience.

HR Operations, HRIS & Payroll Support
Support employee records and HRIS maintenance by partnering collaboratively with HRIS and Payroll on data integrity, routine system updates, reporting, and keeping organizational charts accurate and up to date.
Support time and labor administration by assisting with reviewing attendance records, monitoring timekeeping data, tracking call-offs/absences, and helping respond to basic employee and manager inquiries.
Assist with timekeeping accuracy by helping enter, review, and validate timekeeping data to support the team in ensuring overall payroll accuracy. Serve as a backup payroll processor and participate in shared payroll processing responsibilities with other HR team members to ensure continuity of operations.
Coordinate employee status changes, transfers, compliance reporting, personnel file administration, and employee service anniversary recognition programs.

Compliance, Process Improvement & Projects
Support compliance with federal, state, and local employment laws, assisting with employee handbook updates and policy communications.
Participate in cross-functional HR projects related to compensation, benefits, performance management, and organizational development.
Assist in collecting and compiling basic workforce data (such as turnover, staffing levels, recruiting activity, and attendance) to support reporting and analysis by HR leadership.
Recommend and support continuous process improvements to enhance operational efficiency and the employee experience.

Employee Relations & Employee Support
Serve as an HR point of contact for employees and managers, providing clear guidance on HR policies, procedures, and routine workplace concerns.
Partner with HR leadership to guide and assist managers through performance management, employee coaching, document preparation, and corrective action processes.
Participate in and support employee relations investigations, learning to independently conduct objective inquiries, document findings, and recommend fair resolutions under the guidance of the HR Director.
Help track and evaluate employee relations trends and feedback across departments, collaborating with HR leadership to propose ideas for improving retention, engagement, and workplace culture.

Shared HR Team Responsibilities
Provide timely support for employee and manager HR inquiries.
Collaborate with HR team members to ensure consistent service delivery and departmental coverage.
Cross-train in key HR functions to support business continuity during absences, peak periods, and special projects.
Maintain strict confidentiality of employee and organizational information.
Contribute to a collaborative, service-oriented Human Resources team environment.
Participate in special projects and cross-functional initiatives and other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

Required
Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or a related field
Minimum of three (3) years of progressive Human Resources experience in a Generalist or comparable HR role
Experience supporting core HR functions including onboarding, recruitment, timekeeping, attendance tracking, and HR administration
Working knowledge of federal, state, and local employment laws and HR best practices
Strong verbal and written communication skills, including a "seeking to understand" approach when listening, communicating with employees, and facilitating group presentations or orientations.
Experience working with HRIS platforms and maintaining employee data
Willingness and capability to complete cross-training and serve as a backup payroll processor
Strong judgment and decision-making skills, with the ability to handle confidential information with discretion and professionalism
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment while maintaining high attention to detail

Preferred
Professional HR certification (SHRM-CP, PHR, SHRM-SCP, or SPHR)
Experience in the insurance industry or another highly regulated corporate environment
Hands-on experience with Paylocity or similar HRIS and payroll software
Prior experience supporting university recruiting, career fairs, or managing internship programs

Benefits
Health, dental and vision insurance from day one
Company-funded health savings account (HSA)
Life insurance, short and long-term disability insurance
401(k) with employer match
Paid time off, including summer hours and paid parental leave
Hybrid work location
And much more!

About Us

With 100+ years of history behind every client relationship, we’ve built a reputation on integrity, expertise, and the dedication of our people. That commitment has earned us recognition as a Top Insurance Employer and Top Insurance Workplace by Insurance Business America, a spot among the Top 100 Independent Insurance Agencies by Insurance Journal, and distinction as a leading Northeast Ohio agency by Crain’s Cleveland Business.

Founded in Akron, OH in 1910, we’ve grown to 275+ employees across 24+ locations in Ohio, Kentucky and Florida, while maintaining the personal, relationship driven service that sets us apart.

If you’re passionate about service, enjoy working with people, and want to build a rewarding career with a company that values both professional achievement and personal fulfillment, you’ll thrive at SeibertKeck Insurance Partners.

Our competitive edge comes from:
Regional specialization and deep market knowledge
Client education that emphasizes prevention over reaction
Access to regional, national, and international insurance markets
A reliable in-house claims service team that advocates for clients when it matters most

At SeibertKeck Insurance Partners, we go beyond premium. We reduce costs through proprietary risk-management and loss-control strategies, negotiate the best possible rates through strong carrier relationships, and support clients with responsive, around-the-clock claims partners.

We’re proud of where we’ve been, and even more excited about where we’re going!

jobs.title: Client Support Specialist - Insurance
jobs.body:
Client Support Specialist – Standard Commercial Lines

Location: Ohio, Kentucky or Florida
Employment Type: Full-Time, Hybrid, based in one of our locations (including Medina)

Why Join Us?
Build a rewarding career in the commercial insurance industry with opportunities for growth and advancement.
Work in a supportive, collaborative environment focused on teamwork and exceptional client service.
Take advantage of ongoing training, licensing support, and continuing education opportunities.
Gain valuable experience with commercial insurance operations, carrier systems, and diverse client accounts.
Develop your technical insurance expertise while expanding your professional skills and industry knowledge.

Position Summary
We are seeking a Client Support Specialist who provides administrative and technical support to the Commercial Lines Department by assisting with the daily processing of incoming and outgoing business activities. This position partners closely with Commercial Account Managers and Producers to deliver prompt, efficient, and high-quality service to clients while ensuring the accuracy of policy servicing, documentation, and account maintenance.

The ideal candidate is an experienced Commercial Lines professional who possesses strong attention to detail, excellent communication skills, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a deadline-driven environment.

Essential Responsibilities
Process policy audits received from carriers and refer items to the Commercial Account Manager (CAM) when applicable, following agency audit procedures.
Review and process endorsements and policy change requests for accuracy after they have been ordered by the CAM, including carrier follow-up as needed.
Prepare endorsement summaries and supporting documentation.
Assist Account Managers with pre-renewal marketing activities.
Process and review renewal policies for accuracy and completeness.
Prepare renewal certificates of insurance and basic new certificates as directed by the CAM.
Update policy information, billing screens, company commissions, producer codes, company codes, and status codes within agency management systems.
Process agency-billed invoices related to endorsements and audits.
Obtain, organize, and file electronic documents from carrier websites into ImageRight.
Assist in developing initial client proposals for review by the Account Manager.
Navigate carrier websites to obtain renewals, endorsements, invoices, policy documents, and other account-related information.
Maintain accurate client records and policy documentation in accordance with agency standards and procedures.
Provide timely and professional support to Account Managers, Producers, carriers, and clients.

Qualifications

Education and Experience
High school diploma or GED required.
Minimum of two (2) years of Commercial Lines Property & Casualty insurance experience.
Current and active Ohio Property & Casualty (P&C) License required.

Professional Development
Maintain a current Ohio P&C License.
Participate in continuing education and insurance-related professional development, such as CISR, CIC, or similar industry designation programs.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Strong understanding of commercial insurance policies, coverages, endorsements, renewals, and audits.
Ability to review certificate holder requirements and verify applicable policy coverages.
Knowledge of certificate wording requirements and the ability to coordinate with insureds regarding required coverage additions, quotations, and compliance needs.
Exceptional attention to detail with the ability to identify missing coverages, coverage gaps, and policy discrepancies.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Excel and Word.
Proficient in AMS360, ImageRight, internet research, and carrier web portals.
Ability to effectively navigate multiple carrier websites to obtain policy documents, invoices, endorsements, and renewal information.
Strong analytical, organizational, and decision-making skills.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Professional demeanor and commitment to delivering exceptional customer service.
Ability to adapt to changing priorities while adhering to agency guidelines, procedures, and service standards.
Ability to work independently, prioritize competing responsibilities, and manage a high-volume workload with accuracy and efficiency.

Benefits

jobs.title: Orthodontic Assistant
jobs.body:
At Mellion Orthodontics, we are a busy, highly respected and quality-oriented orthodontic practice that utilizes the latest technology to provide exceptional treatment and service to our patients. We are patient focused and team driven.

Our team at Mellion Orthodontics strives to give our patients the best orthodontic care while providing a fun and unique patient experience. Drs. Zach, Alex and Joe are experts on growth, facial development, teeth and jaw alignment, and our practice is limited to orthodontics and dentofacial orthopedics. We are a family of orthodontists and want to make you feel like family, too. Mellion Orthodontics is proud to be the top Invisalign® provider in Northeast Ohio and our doctors are in the top 1% of all Invisalign® providers worldwide.

We are currently seeking to fill the part-time role of an Orthodontic Assistant in our Medina office which involves direct patient care with a variety of responsibilities that help our patients achieve great smiles with Invisalign® and braces. To the right person, we offer a fun, challenging and rewarding career that offers great work-life balance. Check us out at www.mellionortho.com as well as on Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube & TikTok (@mellionsmiles).

Applicants should fully complete the application to be considered for this position. Incomplete applications will not be reviewed.
**Once you have completed your application, please be sure to check your junk/spam folders; your phone interview invitation may have been directed there.**

If you're the right candidate, you:
Thrive on a fast-paced environment and positivity
Are passionate about customer service and serve our patients and families with a smile, compassion and sense of urgency
Demonstrate attention to detail and ask questions to ensure accuracy
Work independently to achieve team goals and can quickly change course to do what is best for the team
Value your time and the time of others to keep patient appointments on schedule
Appreciate and contribute to a spotless work environment, ensuring the health and safety of all who step foot in our office
Seek a permanent, part-time position (approximately 24-30 hours/week)

Job responsibilities may include but are not limited to:
Communicating clearly with patients and parents
Scheduling appointments
Taking detailed, accurate notes of patient visits
Educating patients on and demonstrating proper oral hygiene techniques and wearing elastics or Invisalign aligners
Assisting the doctor in orthodontic procedures (arch-wire changes, placing and debonding of braces, placing Invisalign attachments, taking dental X-rays, capturing intraoral and facial photographs, and intraoral scans with iTero scanner, etc.)
Sterilization of instruments and infection prevention throughout treatment area and office
Learning to anticipate needs of doctor and teammates to ensure an efficient workflow throughout the day
Organizing and restocking treatment and storage areas
Other responsibilities as needed

Qualifications:
Experience in healthcare, dental or orthodontics preferred but not required; we will train the right candidate
Comfortable using computers and other office technology
Applicants are a minimum age of 18 years old

Other details:
24-30 hours per week; no regular weekend/ evening hours; Our team participates in approximately 3-4 'off hours' events each year including a Continuing Education event (one weeknight), Kylie Rose's Run (one Sunday afternoon) and Greater Medina Chamber of Commerce events (one weeknight).
Monthly and annual bonus opportunity

$18.50 per hour, for those without experience; hourly rate adjusted based on experience

jobs.title: Legal Secretary – Hoffee & Wallace Law Firm (Medina, OH)
jobs.body:
Medina, Ohio – Legal Secretary – Hoffee & Wallace Law Firm
Overview: Looking to hire a Legal Secretary for a full-time position in our downtown Medina office. Starting pay is $18.00 per hour. Schedule is Monday through Friday from 8:30 am to 4:30 pm. In person training will take place in our Wooster office for the first 2-3 weeks (length of training depends on prior experience).
Responsibilities: Provide administrative support to one or more attorneys; Draft and proofread legal documents; File, organize, scan, copy, and fax legal documents in a timely manner; Answer phone calls, take notes/messages, and redirect calls when appropriate; Schedule consultations, hearings, meetings, and depositions; Preserve and update case record system; Facilitate meeting of deadlines by keeping agendas and providing reminders; Effectively communicate with witnesses, clients, colleagues, and court personnel; Greet visitors and perform initial screening of clients; Travel occasionally between Wooster and Medina firm offices.**
**Initial training will also require travel to Wooster, Ohio. Must have reliable transportation.
Qualifications: Outstanding time management and written and oral communication skills; Ability to effectively prioritize and meet deadlines; Ability to multitask and be comfortable dealing with a diverse clientele; Proficient typing skills, including Microsoft Office programs, and ability to work with legal technology, court filings systems, and court docket; Ability to work as a team with attorneys and other colleagues; Courteous and professional demeanor in communications with clients and other professionals; Ability to maintain absolute and complete confidentiality of all client information; Reliable transportation.
Benefits: Our office is closed for all major holidays and between the Christmas and New Years holidays. Office has a convenient downtown location in the Medina Square. Benefits include paid time off, sick leave, and employer matched retirement contributions.
How to Apply: E-mail your resume, cover letter, and list of references with contact information to chelsea@hoffeelawfirm.com
Subject Line: HWLF Legal Secretary (Medina)
Deadline: Accepting applications until filled.

jobs.body:
Insurance Sales Representative
Hertvik Insurance Group
Medina, OH 44256

About Us
Hertvik Insurance is a leading independent agency, passionately serving clients nationwide with comprehensive insurance solutions. From auto to commercial, we empower individuals and businesses to secure their future. Join our energetic team committed to delivering unparalleled service, diverse products, and significant savings, making a tangible difference in our clients' lives.

Job Overview
Hertvik Insurance Group is seeking a motivated, results-driven Sales Representative to join our Personal Lines team. This is a high-activity sales role focused exclusively on warm, referral-based leads. You'll be connecting with people who are actively purchasing a home and have a real, immediate need for homeowners insurance. Your job is simple: work the lead, earn their trust, quote the right coverage, and close the sale. Once the policy is sold, our service team takes it from there so you can stay focused on selling.

Benefits
Annual Base Salary + Commission + Bonus Opportunities
Paid Time Off (PTO)
Flexible Schedule
Health Insurance
Dental Insurance
Vision Insurance
Hands on Training
Disability Insurance
Life Insurance
Career Growth Opportunities
Retirement Plan
Requirements
One of the following is required:

Active Ohio Property & Casualty insurance license OR
Demonstrated sales experience (any industry) with a track record of meeting or exceeding goals; and willingness to obtain P&C licensure upon hire.

Additionally:
Strong phone presence and interpersonal communication skills.
Comfortable working with CRM, AI and quoting technology platforms.
Self-motivated with the ability to manage a high volume of leads independently.
Organized and detail-oriented; able to accurately document activity and follow a defined sales process.
Competitive, goal-oriented mindset with a genuine desire to help customers protect their homes.
Responsibilities
Receive and promptly follow up on warm inbound leads generated through our home closing partner network.
Engage prospective customers via phone, text, email, and other communication channels to understand their insurance needs.
Utilize agency technology tools to manage leads, track activity, and move prospects through the sales pipeline.
Present coverage options and obtain agreement from prospects to receive a quote.
Prepare and deliver accurate personal lines insurance quotes.
Close sales and transition new policyholders to the service team for ongoing account management.
Meet or exceed individual sales goals and activity metrics.
Maintain accurate records of all lead activity and client interactions in agency systems.

Workforce Development Specialist
Jobs for Ohio's Graduates (JOG)

Schedule: Full-Time | Monday–Friday | 8:00 AM–4:30 PM

Jobs for Ohio's Graduates (JOG) is dedicated to helping young people complete their education and successfully transition into meaningful employment or post-secondary training. Through mentorship, career readiness, work experience, and life skills training, JOG empowers youth to overcome barriers and achieve long-term success.

Position Overview
As a Workforce Development Specialist, you will mentor and support youth as they work toward educational, career, and personal goals. This role focuses on building relationships, removing barriers, and connecting participants with employment and training opportunities.

Key Responsibilities
Mentor and coach youth as they transition into employment or post-secondary education.
Help participants identify and overcome barriers to success.
Assess participant needs and develop individualized goal plans.
Teach employability, life skills, and workforce readiness competencies.
Track participant progress and maintain accurate documentation.
Build relationships with employers, schools, and community partners.
Collaborate with the JOG team to ensure participant success.
Promote JOG's mission, standards, and program objectives.

Qualifications
Bachelor's degree required.
Experience working with youth required.
Strong communication and relationship-building skills.
Proficient in:Microsoft Outlook
Microsoft Word
Microsoft Excel
Microsoft PowerPoint
Online database management systems

Ability to travel locally during the day within a five-county service area.
Valid driver's license and reliable transportation preferred.

Benefits
Medical Insurance
Dental Insurance
Vision Insurance
Life Insurance
401(k) Retirement Plan
401(k) Company Match
Paid Time Off (PTO)
Employee Assistance Program (EAP)

Make a meaningful impact in the lives of young people.
Help youth overcome barriers and achieve their goals.

Build strong partnerships with schools, employers, and community organizations while changing lives every day.
